question: Name the physico-chemical process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods with the help of chlorophyll.
 
• During photosynthesis, plants convert light energy into chemical energy that is stored in glucose, a type of sugar.
 
• The process primarily takes place in the chloroplasts of plant cells, which contain the pigment chlorophyll.
 
• Photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth as it is the primary source of all organic matter for nearly all organisms, and it also releases oxygen into the atmosphere as a by-product.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorophyll**: This is the green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plant cells that is crucial for photosynthesis. It captures light energy from the sun.
 
• **Light Reactions**: The first stage of photosynthesis where light energy is captured and used to produce ATP and NADPH, which are energy carriers.
 
• **Calvin Cycle**: The second stage of photosynthesis, also known as the dark reactions, where ATP and NADPH produced in the light reactions are used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
 
• **Stomata**: Small openings on the surface of leaves that allow for gas exchange. They play a crucial role in photosynthesis by allowing carbon dioxide to enter and oxygen to leave the plant.
